item.title: Monetary Policy Decision Press Conference Opening Statement

rating.summary: Bank of Canada Governor Tiff Macklem announced the decision to hold the policy rate at 2.25%, citing broadly in-line economic data since July, a broadening recovery with Q2 GDP growth of 3.3%, and unemployment edging down to 6.4%. The statement highlighted two-sided risks: new US tariffs adding uncertainty to the growth outlook, while persistently high energy prices from Middle East conflict have increased upside risks to inflation. The overall tone was balanced with a slight hawkish tilt due to heightened inflation risks.
rating.stance_rationale: The hold decision is neutral, but the explicit acknowledgment of increased upside inflation risks from energy prices and tariff pass-through, combined with the absence of any easing bias, gives the statement a mildly hawkish lean. Core inflation near 2% and excess supply temper a stronger hawkish signal.
key_quotes: The longer oil prices and refinery margins stay high, the greater the risk that higher energy prices spill over and turn into persistent inflation.
The upside risks to inflation have increased, while new tariffs make growth prospects more uncertain.
